checkerRole: independent content checker (R4 Stage 2 blind full reconstruction)

representation.STAGE: proposedBoundary == exact declared stage id string

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: Baseline supplies everything the choice needs: the case summary states the stool test is positive for C. difficile toxin, and the assessment records eight to ten loose foul-smelling stools daily after a completed clindamycin course, with a semiprivate room. Contact precautions for a spore-forming enteric pathogen follow, and droplet, airborne and protective isolation are excluded by the same facts.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: The single declared stage states only 'Initiate appropriate transmission-based precautions' without naming a category, so it neither supplies nor discloses the answer. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: Baseline establishes a toxin-positive C. difficile infection, and the answer is spore knowledge: alcohol-based rub does not remove spores, so hand hygiene after care requires soap and water. Rinsing with water alone, using rub only, or layering gloves over rub all fail on the same point.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_orders refers to 'Stool and surface infection-prevention measures per protocol' without specifying a hand-hygiene method. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: Each row states its own student action, and baseline establishes toxin-positive C. difficile in a semiprivate room. Gowning and gloving before entry, dedicated single-client equipment, and removing personal protective equipment with hand hygiene before leaving are correct, while cleaning with a quaternary-ammonium wipe alone requires correction because it is not sporicidal.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_orders mentions surface measures per protocol but names no product or technique. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The doffing sequence is standard personal-protective-equipment practice - gloves, then eye protection, then gown, then hand hygiene - and baseline supplies the one case-specific element, that the final hand hygiene must use soap and water because the organism is C. difficile.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_orders states no doffing sequence. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem scopes the item explicitly to the 0800 triage presentation, which is the single baseline exhibit, and all four rows are quoted from it: temperature 104.2 F, diffuse anterior neck enlargement, severe agitation with orientation to person only, and a heart rate of 152. Separating the goitre as a feature of uncomplicated hyperthyroidism from the hyperpyrexia, encephalopathy and extreme tachycardia that mark decompensation is endocrine knowledge.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: The later stages carry the treatment orders and the noon laboratory results; neither contains a triage finding or assigns a category. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The option set names all four agents, so the drugs to be sequenced are inside the part, and baseline establishes thyroid storm with a heart rate of 152 and a temperature of 104.2 in a client who stopped methimazole three weeks ago. The order is thyroid-storm pharmacology: a beta blocker first for the adrenergic crisis, a thionamide before iodine so the iodine does not fuel new hormone synthesis, then the corticosteroid.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_0830 is the order set the stem refers to; it lists the medications but states no administration sequence or rationale. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: Baseline supplies the hypermetabolic picture the interventions address - temperature 104.2, profuse diaphoresis, extreme agitation and tachycardia - and each option is decided by knowledge: external cooling, a cool quiet low-stimulation environment, acetaminophen and seizure precautions are indicated, while salicylates are avoided because they displace thyroid hormone from binding proteins, and fluid restriction is wrong in a hypermetabolic, diaphoretic client.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: The later stages carry the orders and results; neither states an intervention set. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: All four options state their own laboratory values, so the comparison is inside the part, and the stem names the drug whose adverse effect is being monitored. Recognising a white blood cell count of 2.8 as the agranulocytosis signal requiring immediate notification, while a normal urea, a normal potassium and a still-elevated free T4 do not, is propylthiouracil pharmacology.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_1200 is the source of the values the options restate, and it flags none of them. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem scopes the item to the initial triage assessment, and every option is drawn from baseline: the case summary records crushing substernal pain radiating to the jaw and arm with visible diaphoresis, and the triage exhibit records a heart rate of 110, 4 mm ST elevation in V1 through V4, and a saturation of 92 percent on room air. Selecting the infarct-plus-sympathetic-activation cluster while excluding the mild desaturation is knowledge applied to that surface.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_1415 carries the later arrest; it contains no triage finding. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem states the event itself - sudden unresponsiveness with a chaotic rhythm on the monitor - and the option set names the four actions. Sequencing a call for the team and defibrillator, immediate high-quality compressions, unsynchronised defibrillation, then epinephrine is resuscitation-algorithm knowledge requiring no case data beyond the stem.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_1415 is where the arrest occurs, and the stem restates it; the stage states no sequence. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: All four rows name a medication and all four columns name a classification, so the matching runs entirely on pharmacology knowledge - amiodarone as antiarrhythmic, epinephrine as vasopressor, aspirin as antiplatelet, nitroglycerin as vasodilator. Baseline supplies only the clinical relevance of the agents through the STEMI presentation.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_1415 narrates the resuscitation in which these agents are used; it assigns no classification. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: All four options state their own finding, so the comparison is inside the part, and the discrimination is physiology: an abrupt sustained rise in end-tidal carbon dioxide to 40 mmHg is the most definitive evidence of restored circulation, while an organised rhythm without a pulse is pulseless electrical activity, and dilated unreactive pupils and agonal gasps are not evidence of return of circulation.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_1415 narrates the resuscitation and its outcome; it names no confirmatory sign. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem scopes the item explicitly to the 1400 triage assessment, and all five rows are drawn from baseline: temperature 102.0 F, heart rate 118, blood pressure 94/52, altered mental status with orientation to person only, and the diabetes history from the case summary. Sorting temperature and heart rate as inflammatory-response criteria, hypotension and altered mentation as organ dysfunction, and a chronic comorbidity as neither is knowledge.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_1600 carries the later course; it contains no triage finding and classifies nothing. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem states the premise, that septic shock is confirmed, and the option set names the four actions. Sequencing the weight-based crystalloid bolus, cultures, antibiotics and then vasopressor support is sepsis-bundle knowledge, and baseline supplies the hypotension and hypoperfusion that make the bolus the opening move.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_1600 narrates the interventions being delivered; it states no sequence. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: Every option states its own finding and value, and baseline supplies the pre-treatment comparators that make them readable as improvement - blood pressure 94/52, orientation to person only, and dark cloudy concentrated urine with decreased output. Recognising a mean arterial pressure of 70, urine output of 40 mL per hour, improved orientation and a falling lactate as improvement, while cool clammy skin and an unchanged creatinine are not, is evaluation.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_1600 is the source of the post-resuscitation values, which the options restate, and it classifies none of them. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem states the entire clinical situation - a mean arterial pressure still at 60 on norepinephrine at 10 mcg/min with vasopressin added - and the rationale is vasopressor pharmacology: vasopressin is a catecholamine-sparing adjunct that permits a lower norepinephrine dose and reduces peripheral ischaemia, rather than an inotrope or a beta-1 agonist.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_1600 carries the escalation the stem restates; it states no rationale. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.
